newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia says digitals high in handset sales.
newsitem.headline: Nokia says digitals high in handset sales.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Thursday the share of digital handsets in its mobile phone sales was above the industry average.
"Of the global total (in the industry) sold last year perhaps 52 percent were digital, for us it was closer to 60 percent," CEO Jorma Ollila told a news conference on Nokia's results.
He said Nokia's mobile phones unit had recovered faster than expected from problems in the first half of last year.
"Mobile Phones returned to strong growth and healthy margins, even slightly faster than we expected," he said.
Ollila said its 9000 Communicator, combining a laptop computer with a mobile phone, had sold "as well as expected" and Nokia had been able to "hold the price very well".
"In about three or four months after we launched the product we have recovered all the R&D expenditure in this business area for this product, and for other products in cellular data," Ollila said.
"It is now approaching a mass launch...so mass production will be started, it takes about six months to get the ramp up for a difficult product like that."
Ollila said he expected the Cebit industry fair this year to bring competiton to the Communicator, but added that this would help make a market for such products.
Asked if the world total of mobile phone subscribers could rise above 500 million in 2001, Ollila said: "It starts with a four or could be higher".

Nokia's rival Ericsson earlier this week forecast mobile phone subscribers worldwide would rise to 480 million by 2000, with digital handset subscribers reaching 500 million by 2001. Ollila declined to give a specific forecast.
He said cellular phone penetration tended to accelerate at levels above 15 percent, if the infrastructure was good enough.
"We expect that rule more or less applies," Ollila said.
